subject: Coordination: incident notification obligations & timeline confirmation
messages:
From: security@finexcorp.com
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jane.parker@finexcorp.com
Date: 2026-11-01T08:15:00Z
Subject: Potential data exposure affecting FinexCorp integration — initial report

Olga / Redwood security team,

We wanted to flag a potential data exposure that affects our integration. Over the last 36 hours we observed anomalous API calls from an IP range that maps back to credentials provisioned to our Redwood integration. At this stage we are treating this as "suspected unauthorized access" to logs and possibly customer identifiers.

High-level:
- Affected scope: API keys used by FinexCorp integration; may include hashed user IDs and metadata (no payment data observed yet).
- Time window: ~2026-10-30 14:00 UTC to 2026-10-31 06:00 UTC
- First detection: 2026-11-01 06:40 UTC (automated anomaly alert)

We need to coordinate on the notification scope and timelines under the DPA and applicable EU privacy rules. Please provide:
1) Redwood's initial notification commitment window if unauthorized access is confirmed.
2) What evidence (logs, signed statements, redacted samples) you can provide for our audit team.
3) Contact for escalation to legal/counsel.

Attaching a one-page incident_summary_20261101.pdf with redacted indicators. We would like an initial status update within 48 hours.

Jane Parker
Head of Security Operations, FinexCorp
security@finexcorp.com

Attachments: incident_summary_20261101.pdf
From: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
To: security@finexcorp.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure affecting FinexCorp integration — initial report

Jane — thanks for the heads up and for the summary. We take this seriously. High level acknowledgement below and immediate next steps from our side.

Acknowledgement & initial stance:
- We received your report and will treat this as a suspected unauthorized access incident pending our forensic review.
- Redwood's DPA (Section 5.2) defines an initial notification to the data controller within 72 hours of confirmation of unauthorized access. We will prioritize containment and evidence collection first.

Immediate ask to FinexCorp:
- Can you confirm whether the API keys in question were scoped to production customer data or sandbox/test environments?
- Please share the redacted sample of any customer identifiers you believe are affected (if available) so we can quickly match logs.

What Redwood will provide within the first update:
- Confirmation of whether we confirm unauthorized access within 72 hours of our validation.
- A redacted log extract (timestamps + request paths, no raw payloads) and a signed incident summary for your compliance file.
- If cross-border data movement is relevant, we will indicate the data transfer paths and subprocessors involved.

Proposed cadence:
- Initial acknowledgement (this email): within 4 hours of report.
- Technical status update: within 48 hours with preliminary scope and evidence snippet.
- Legal/contractual notification (if access is confirmed and meets notification criteria): within 72 hours per DPA obligations, with follow-up 10-day remediation summary.

Please let us know if FinexCorp requires a faster SLA (you requested 48 hours). We can provide a 48-hour preliminary update but need to lock down on the scope and evidence requirements.

I'm looping Marcus (ops lead) and Monica (incident response) and Rishi (privacy counsel) to coordinate tasks — we'll set a bridge shortly.

—Olga
Olga Petrov | Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

> I'm looping Marcus (ops lead) and Monica (incident response) and Rishi (privacy counsel) to coordinate tasks — we'll set a bridge shortly.

Team — quick ops checklist and owners (aiming for a 48-hour preliminary technical update):
- Marcus (me): Triage and containment — identify credential rotation needs, revoke impacted API keys, and issue temporary tokens.
- Monica: Forensics — extract KV cache access logs, inference request metadata, and request path summaries for the specified window. Provide redacted extracts for external sharing.
- Rishi: Legal/privacy — advise on notification language, DPA trigger thresholds, and cross-border transfer implications.
- Olga: External coordination and timeline commitments.

Evidence we'll prepare for FinexCorp (examples):
- Redacted request logs (timestamps, path, response code) — CSV snippet
- Signed statement of confirmed scope or statement of "no evidence of unauthorized exfiltration" if not found
- List of subprocessors that handled the relevant request paths and any cross-border hops

Notes on transfer & subprocessors:
- If data touched our EU edge, we will include EU subprocessors (CloudStorage-EU, LogIngestor) and state whether Standard Contractual Clauses apply for onward transfers.

I'll schedule a 30-min bridge at 14:00 UTC to align on tasks and finalize the 48-hour update.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Head of Incident Response

Olga/Team — thanks for the quick coordination and proposed plan. Quick answers and what FinexCorp is requesting: 

Finex answers:
- Environment: production API keys (confirmed) — customer identifiers may be referenced in URI parameters.
- We attached access_logs_snippet.zip that shows the anomalous calls and sample identifiers (pseudonymized).

Finex requests from Redwood (urgent):
1) Written confirmation within 48 hours on whether Redwood confirms unauthorized access to production systems. If Redwood cannot confirm within 48 hours, an interim technical status update is requested.
2) Redacted logs and a signed incident summary for our audit folder (we will accept redacted CSV + signed PDF).
3) List of subprocessors that processed the requests and any third-country transfers.
4) Contact for escalation to Redwood legal: we have counsel on standby (counsel@vendorlaw.com).

We appreciate the proposed 72-hour DPA window but because this affects live customer data, our internal policy requires a 48-hour initial confirm/interim update. Please confirm you can provide an interim update at 48 hours and we will mark FinexCorp critical.

Attachments: access_logs_snippet.zip

Jane Parker
Head of Security Operations, FinexCorp
